groups.cause: capitalisation/homograph — the popup resolved the opposite member of a deliberately taught minimal pair
groups.currentAuthored: { de: 'Deutsch', pos: 'language' } AND { de: 'deutsch', pos: 'adjective' } — an intentional contrast pair
groups.renderedVsPopup: span = adjective amber (correct for lower-case deutsch); popup headword = object green, i.e. it resolved the capitalised language noun Deutsch
groups.grammaticalTruth: lower-case deutsch is the nationality adjective; capitalised Deutsch is the language noun. The chapter teaches exactly this distinction and lists it as a top A1 mistake (line 439: "The language is a noun — capitalise it. Lower-case deutsch is the adjective.").
groups.proposedCorrection: make headword resolution case-respecting for this pair so lower-case deutsch resolves to the adjective entry. Data-side option: give the adjective entry a distinguishing key/alias so it wins for the lower-case surface. Do NOT equalise the colours — the colours are semantically correct on each side; the wrong lexeme is being picked.
groups.confidence: PROVEN (both entries exist in source; the chapter states the distinction explicitly)
groups.required: REQUIRED — highest pedagogical priority: the popup contradicts the chapter’s own headline teaching point
groups.expectedQaImpact: 4 HCM resolve; no other code affected (no CASE_COLLISION finding fires on these nodes)

groups.cause: capitalisation/homograph — sentence-initial verb resolved as the plural noun
groups.sourceField: vocab entry (line 259) { de: 'zahlen', pos: 'verb', ex: 'Zahlen, bitte!' } and the phrase table (line 379) 'Zahlen, bitte.'
groups.renderedVsPopup: span = verb red (correct: it is zahlen, "to pay", capitalised only because it opens the utterance); popup headword = object green, i.e. it resolved die Zahlen ("the numbers")
groups.grammaticalTruth: "Zahlen, bitte!" = the verb zahlen. die Zahlen (numbers) is an unrelated lexeme.
groups.proposedCorrection: case/context-aware resolution for the sentence-initial verb, or an explicit token role for the phrase-table cell. Colours are individually correct; the lexeme choice is wrong.
groups.confidence: PROVEN (source entry and phrase context both read)

groups.cause: non-grammatical entity — a single letter carrying a grammar role in prose
groups.sourceField: no authored token — auto-linkified from vocabulary text (grep for a Fuß/letter token in a1-39 data returned no match)
groups.renderedVsPopup: span = adverb cyan; popup headword = --ink-secondary, which chapter-app.js:2022 ROLE_COLOR_VAR assigns deliberately to letter|name|conjunction entries
groups.grammaticalTruth: the popup side is CORRECT by design. The defect is the prose span: a bare letter should not be coloured as an adverb.
groups.proposedCorrection: exclude the single letter from role colouring (or author it as a letter token) so it renders in neutral ink like its popup.
groups.confidence: PROVEN for the head side (source-identified mapping); STRONGLY SUGGESTED that the span is simply mis-guessed
groups.required: OPTIONAL — lowest impact of the 18: one letter in one vocabulary list, no grammatical claim is contradicted
